name: Nevada
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+.
summary: Nevada voters approved medical cannabis in 2000 and adult-use legalization in 2016, with retail sales starting July 1, 2017. Since January 1, 2024, adults can buy and possess up to 2.5 ounces of flower or a quarter ounce of concentrate. Public consumption is banned except in licensed consumption lounges, and home growing is allowed only for people living more than 25 miles from a dispensary.

medical_since.value: Voters approved medical cannabis in 2000; dispensaries were authorized in 2014.

possession_limit.value: Up to 2.5 ounces of flower or 1/4 ounce of concentrate, raised from 1 ounce and 1/8 ounce by SB 277 effective January 1, 2024.

home_grow.value: Only for adults living at least 25 miles from the nearest dispensary: up to 6 plants per person and 12 per household, out of public view.

public_use.value: Illegal in public except in licensed consumption lounges; public use can bring a fine of up to $600.

taxes.value: 10% retail excise tax on adult-use sales, with proceeds going to the State Education Fund, plus sales tax.

regulator.value: Nevada Cannabis Compliance Board (CCB), created by AB 533 in 2019.

timeline.event: AB 533 creates the Cannabis Compliance Board.
SB 277 raises possession and purchase limits to 2.5 ounces of flower and 1/4 ounce of concentrate.

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older, including visitors, can buy and possess cannabis, and medical cannabis has been legal since 2000.

faq.q: How much weed can you buy in Nevada?
faq.a: Up to 2.5 ounces of flower or a quarter ounce of concentrate, under limits that took effect January 1, 2024.

faq.q: Can you smoke weed in Las Vegas in public?
faq.a: No. Public consumption is illegal and can bring a fine; use is allowed in private residences with permission and in licensed consumption lounges.

faq.q: Can you grow weed in Nevada?
faq.a: Only if you live at least 25 miles from the nearest dispensary, up to 6 plants per adult and 12 per household.
